R8A-bear-atv-0002.name: By Smith Creek
R8A-bear-atv-0002.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R8A-bear-atv-0002.parkWhat: where the truck road ends (Willis Creek); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle)

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2020 (6 years old), 110 m SE: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2018 (fire K62690), 100 m SE: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
W facing slope, 11 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Smith Creek 70 m SW: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Town of Princeton, about 25 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Copper Mountain Rd, Willis Creek FSR, Willis Creek.
Park: 49.28248, -120.28318, where the truck road ends (Willis Creek); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle). Map links below.
Ride: 1.4 km on P51100 - Smith Creek by ATV (all terrain vehicle) or 4x4 on rough road, estimate. Then walk 60 m S, climb about 0 m.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 8-4, Region 8. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-01, closures 2026-10-16.
